**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, or usage-verification right binding Sparkling. Section 3 imposes use restrictions but pairs them with no verification mechanic, no reporting obligation, and no vendor access to our systems or premises. The only examination right in the document runs in our favour (§ 16 escrow verification).

Because there is no vendor audit right at all, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation, or system-access exposure to constrain — this sits better than the playbook's preferred position, so no insertion is warranted. Volunteering audit machinery here would only create an exposure that does not currently exist.

Negotiation note for the file: if Garman later proposes a usage-verification or audit right, it should be held to the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access), with the 15-day-notice / 10% fallback available if pressed.
